sections.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
sections.abstract: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) are an emerging population of high-energy transients with diverse physical origins. Only a few observed EFXTs are associated with compact object mergers, and the known events generally display X-ray emission lasting much longer than their associated short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Here we report EP260411a, an $\sim8$-s EFXT discovered in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope (EP-WXT) observations through a time-targeted search for X-ray counterparts of short GRBs. This fast X-ray transient is temporally coincident with short GRB 260411A, with both the pulse width and peak time showing clear anticorrelations with the characteristic photon energy across the gamma-ray and soft X-ray bands. Joint EP-WXT and Fermi-GBM spectral fitting further shows that the broadband emission can be described by a cutoff power-law model with an additional low-energy spectral break, suggesting a common origin for the single-pulse X-ray and gamma-ray emission. The resulting properties place the event within the Type I GRB region in the $E_{\rm p,z}$-$E_{\rm iso}$ plane, supporting its classification as a compact object merger event. Unlike previously known merger-driven Type I EFXTs with long-lasting X-ray emission, EP260411a reveals that the Type I EFXT population can also extend to the short timescale of a few seconds. Its combination of short duration and hard spectrum occupies a sparsely explored region of the EFXT parameter space, providing a new observational link between short-duration EFXTs and compact object mergers.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify EP260411a in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope data, temporally coincident with GRB 260411A; joint EP-WXT/Fermi-GBM spectral fitting and its position in the Type-I GRB relation support, but do not prove, a merger origin.
sections.evidence_type: observational; archival Einstein Probe EP-WXT search, Fermi-GBM gamma-ray data, joint spectral fits, and ZTF follow-up constraints.
sections.unique_caveat: It is one event; the roughly 3-arcminute localization and incomplete galaxy catalog leave no unique host or precise redshift, limiting the progenitor classification.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A separate report highlighted the Einstein Probe event; Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot, so placement rests on the unusual observed event and independent coverage, not citation momentum.

sections.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Enhancing deep-learning models: the impact of image processing and training data selection for strong-lens detection
sections.abstract: Euclid is expected to discover ~$10^5$ galaxy-galaxy strong gravitational lenses across ~14,000deg$^2$, requiring automated searches with high completeness and low false-positive rates. Despite advances in deep learning, the effects of training-set composition, image representation, and preprocessing on survey-scale detection remain poorly understood. We present an ablation study of the convolutional neural network used in the ECLIPSE strong-lens detection pipeline, evaluating different training configurations on a fixed test set. Using simulated and real Euclid data, we compare VIS-only and pseudo-RGB representations, FITS and JPEG formats, training-set composition, hard-negative selection, and multi-stage training. We also assess ensembling on ~67 million DR1 cutouts. Training-set composition and strategy strongly affect high-Recall performance. Omitting simulation based pre-training reduces high-Recall weighted average Precision by 83.7% for VIS-only and 74.5% for pseudo-RGB models. Negative-sample selection also substantially affects performance, while FITS yields modest gains over JPEG at high Recall (~2-5%). On DR1, the logit-mean ensemble improves average Precision by 28.0% and 39.9% over the individual VIS-only and pseudo-RGB models. Among ~70,000 candidates selected for visual inspection, it recovers 11,256 unique grade A (secure) and B (probable) lenses, compared with 9650 and 10,395 for the individual models. The branches show complementary ranking preferences, particularly for lenses benefiting from near-infrared information. Careful training-set design, realistic negatives, and multi-band ensembling improve survey-scale searches. Our final ensemble achieves ~80% Recall at the operational selection threshold, outperforming ablation models with higher global classification metrics and highlighting the need to optimise performance for realistic survey conditions.[Abridged]
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that their logit-mean ensemble recovers 11,256 visually graded A/B lens candidates among about 70,000 candidates selected for inspection and reaches about 80% recall at the operational threshold; omitting simulation pre-training sharply reduces high-recall precision.
sections.evidence_type: computational; ConvNeXt-Base ablations using simulated and real Euclid imaging, a fixed test set, and approximately 67 million DR1 cutouts.
sections.unique_caveat: Visual grades include subjective judgments, and conclusions are established for one fully fine-tuned network architecture; transfer to smaller or different models remains untested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete survey-scale evaluation across about 67 million DR1 cutouts, an official Euclid DR1 release, and an INSPIRE record provide corroborating data-release and research signals; this is a pipeline result, not a lens-discovery count.

sections.title: Quantum phase estimation on a Rydberg quantum simulator
sections.abstract: Determining the energy spectrum of a many-body quantum system is a central goal of quantum physics. Ground-state energies underpin materials science and quantum chemistry, whereas excited states govern dynamical phenomena such as quantum thermalization. Quantum simulators have greatly shaped our understanding of many-body systems, for example, by enabling access to microscopic mechanisms and nonlocal order parameters. However, experiments still struggle to access the full range of many-body spectral features and are typically limited to measuring energy gaps and excitations by spectroscopic means. Here, we address this challenge by demonstrating quantum phase estimation on an analog Rydberg quantum simulator. We reconstruct the complex-valued return amplitude, or Loschmidt echo, of an initial probe state. From its Fourier transform, we measure absolute ground-state energies and energy gaps in systems of up to 19 atoms in one and two spatial dimensions. Varying the initial probe state, we select distinct spectral windows within which we compute the longitudinal and transverse magnetization, and observe their competition across the many-body spectrum. Our results thereby demonstrate phase-sensitive many-body spectroscopy on an analog quantum simulator without auxiliary qubits or controlled evolution.
sections.claimed_result: The authors demonstrate statistical quantum phase estimation on an analog Rydberg simulator, reconstructing complex return amplitudes and measuring absolute energies and gaps while selecting spectral windows for magnetization observables.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; analog Rydberg-atom simulator with one- and two-dimensional arrays of up to 19 atoms.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is finite-size; the authors note that Hamiltonian calibration errors shift the energy offset and that this contribution is not included in the reported statistical uncertainties.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A laboratory demonstration of phase-sensitive many-body spectroscopy without auxiliary qubits or controlled evolution, cross-listed in quantum and atomic physics.

sections.title: Turbulence at the Correlation Scale as the Driver of Magnetic Reconnection: In Situ Observations and Kinetic Simulations
sections.abstract: We study the statistical properties of magnetic reconnection using high-resolution in situ observations from the Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) Mission in the terrestrial magnetosheath and kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. For the first time, using in situ observations, we find that the statistics of upstream reconnecting fields in a macroscopic turbulent plasma system are closely linked with the amplitude of turbulence at the correlation scales. These results are further confirmed with fully kinetic plasma turbulence simulations. Consequently, the average magnetic reconnection rates and associated heating rates, determined through the upstream fields, could become orders of magnitude higher than those predicted using the turbulence amplitude at the dissipation scale. We then use a simplified model of the heating of reconnection exhausts to estimate the ratio of this reconnection heating rate to the overall energy cascade rate due to turbulence. Estimates from the PIC simulations and the MMS observations yield a ratio on the order of $1/5$, indicating that direct reconnection heating is playing a substantial role in dissipating the turbulent fluctuations.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find correlation-scale upstream fields predict much higher reconnection rates and heating than estimates based on dissipation-scale amplitudes, and estimate reconnection heating at roughly one-fifth of the turbulence cascade rate.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Magnetospheric Multiscale measurements in the terrestrial magnetosheath, checked with fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations and a simplified exhaust-heating model.
sections.unique_caveat: The heating fraction depends on a simplified exhaust model and the sampled plasma conditions; the estimate is not a direct calorimetric measurement of the global turbulent energy budget.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It combines in-situ MMS measurements with cross-method kinetic-simulation validation and spans plasma and space physics.

sections.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
sections.abstract: The Lyman-$α$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $Ω_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $σ_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $σ_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.
sections.claimed_result: In idealized fully sampled mocks, the joint full-shape analysis yields unbiased parameters and adding the Lyman-alpha bispectrum improves the simulated constraint on σ₈ by 28%; the authors also report additional gains from quasar clustering statistics.
sections.evidence_type: computational; effective-field-theory modeling validated on large-volume Lyman-alpha mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulations at z=2.5.
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted precision comes from idealized mocks and a fully sampled flux field; observational selection, instrumental effects, and nuisance-systematic control must be tested on DESI data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listing between cosmology and high-energy theory, simulation validation with stated precision gains, and an INSPIRE record support its methodological relevance; the reported constraints are simulation results, not DESI measurements.

sections.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) : Performance of the redshift measurement and spectroscopic analysis
sections.abstract: The European Space Agency's Euclid mission has issued its first major data release(Data Release 1, DR1), providing a transformative view of the extragalactic sky through deep photometry and near-infrared slitless spectroscopy. This paper presents the Euclid DR1 spectroscopic data set and details the evolution of the spectroscopic processing function (SPE PF) pipeline, which is responsible for the automated analysis of 1-dimensional spectra acquired by the Near-Infrared Spectro-Photometer (NISP). The SPE PF pipeline workflow comprises spectroscopic classification, redshift determination, and the systematic measurement of spectral features. Emission line fluxes are derived using two independent methodologies: direct integration (DI) and Gaussian fitting (GF). For sources exhibiting broad H$α$ profiles (velocity dispersion larger than $1500$ km s$^{-1}$), a dedicated `QSO mode' is implemented to robustly deconvolve nuclear and host galaxy components. The data set was validated by cross-matching Euclid results with external spectroscopic catalogues, specifically Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR1, and through an extensive visual inspection campaign of approximately 4000 sources within the Euclid Deep Field North (EDF-N). For high-quality samples selected in the EDF-N, we find a 98.5\% agreement between Euclid and DESI spectroscopic redshifts. This success rate increases to 98.9\% when incorporating pipeline probability and reliability estimators. (abridged)
sections.claimed_result: For selected high-quality sources in the Euclid Deep Field North, the authors report 98.5% redshift agreement with DESI DR1, increasing to 98.9% when pipeline probability and reliability estimators are used.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Euclid NISP slitless spectra and SPE processing pipeline, compared with DESI DR1 and visual checks of approximately 4,000 EDF-N sources.
sections.unique_caveat: The quoted agreement is for selected high-quality EDF-N samples, not a guarantee of accuracy for every source or the full DR1 footprint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is part of the same major Euclid DR1 release as paper #2, and the Consortium’s DR1 paper index independently identifies the spectroscopy work; the paper reports a direct external redshift comparison.

sections.title: Gravitational-wave hierarchical inference from population samples
sections.abstract: Standard approaches to gravitational-wave population inference require evaluating the probability density of the population model. While appropriate for models composed of exact functional forms, this approach is not compatible with state-of-the-art astrophysical predictions from population-synthesis codes, which simulate samples from astrophysical models whose densities are unknown. We present an approach that solely requires samples and never density evaluations of the targeted population model. Key technical ingredients include efficient surrogates for the single-event likelihoods and detection probability, together with an efficient sampling strategy. Using detections up to GWTC-5.0, we validate the method against standard inference with a parametric model, showcase its flexibility on a simulated population including hierarchical mergers, and present a realistic application to a grid of astrophysical population-synthesis simulations with five formation channels. This work paves the way toward a direct comparison of astrophysical models and gravitational-wave data.
sections.claimed_result: The authors validate their sample-based method against parametric inference, demonstrate it on simulated hierarchical mergers, and apply it to five formation channels using GWTC-5.0 detections.
sections.evidence_type: computational; gravitational-wave detections, simulated populations, population-synthesis model samples, likelihood and detection-probability surrogates.
sections.unique_caveat: Population conclusions depend on the accuracy of the single-event likelihood and detection-probability surrogates and on the astrophysical models represented in the tested grid.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The sample-only method addresses a concrete obstacle in comparing population-synthesis models with gravitational-wave data, is cross-listed into gravitation, and is indexed by INSPIRE.

sections.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
sections.abstract: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit. Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) reveals the systematic localization of itinerant $d$-quasiparticle states at the Fermi level, consistent with the emergence of a soft Coulomb gap, while the underlying band structure and symmetry are preserved. Transport reveals Efros-Shklovskii variable-range hopping governed by a colossal soft gap with characteristic temperature $T_{\mathrm{ES}}>50{,}000\,\mathrm{K}$ and screened Coulomb interaction strengths as high as 1.6 eV. Together, multiple lines of evidence indicate that interacting Anderson behavior is a native characteristic that survives to temperatures as high as $500\,\mathrm{K}$ in high-entropy materials.
sections.claimed_result: For the studied La-Sr-Mn-Cr-Fe-Co-Ni oxide series, the authors report localization near the Ioffe-Regel limit and transport consistent with Efros-Shklovskii hopping, with behavior persisting to 500 K at the most disordered composition.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; composition-tuned oxide samples studied with angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and electrical transport.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is specific to the studied oxide series and its transport/spectral interpretation; it does not establish room-temperature Anderson behavior as universal across high-entropy materials.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Semantic Scholar listed 0 citations and 0 influential citations at the snapshot; its place is based on complementary ARPES and transport evidence for a tunable correlated-disorder regime, not measured attention.
